documents.title: Academic Affairs Principles for AI
documents.stance_why: The document says "Our goal is not to prescribe a single approach to AI adoption" and that "Faculty members are best positioned to determine whether, when, and how AI tools support the learning objectives", asking faculty to "communicate clear guidance". It sets no default rule and hands the decision to instructors, so delegates.
documents.summary: Academic Affairs principles say AI should support, not replace, learning, and that faculty decide whether and how AI is used in their courses and must communicate this clearly. They add AI literacy (evaluation, bias, environmental cost) and an accountability principle for faculty and students.

units.why: The intro frames the principles as the Academic Affairs foundation, with AI meant to "strengthen — rather than compromise" education. This is an institution-level framework of purpose and scope, so P56.
units.anchor: AI serves to strengthen — rather than compromise or diminish — the educational
units.frag_end: educational experience at the heart of our mission

units.why: The heading "AI is a Tool Used to Support Learning, Not to Replace It" and the line that AI "should complement, not replace, the human effort" direct that AI not take over the learning work. P32 (student stays the thinker) fits; P41 is the skill-building rationale and is used for the next unit.
units.anchor: The use of AI should complement, not replace, the human effort required for meaningful learning.

units.why: "The process of learning — asking questions, wrestling with complexity" is "essential" to growth, giving the reason doing the work yourself matters. That is the skill-building rationale, P41.
units.anchor: The process of learning — asking questions, wrestling with complexity, developing expertise
units.frag_end: essential to intellectual growth and development.

units.why: "AI should be used in ways that serve to strengthen student learning and creativity while preserving the intellectual work" conditions AI use on keeping the work that builds skill. That reason is the skill-building rationale, P41; P32 is used for the adjacent "complement, not replace" sentence.
units.anchor: preserving the intellectual work through which students develop knowledge and skills
units.policy: AI should be used in ways that serve to strengthen student learning and creativity while preserving the intellectual work through which students develop knowledge and skills
units.fit_note: Also frames AI as acceptable when it strengthens learning and creativity, which P41 (limits because the work builds skill) does not state.
units.resolution_why: Coder A: P32 permit with a normalized policy; coder B: P41 restrict, anchor only. The source says AI 'should be used in ways that serve to strengthen student learning and creativity while preserving the intellectual work through which students develop knowledge and skills'. The clause is a condition on use, and its reason is that the work builds skill, which is what P41 covers; P32 is already assigned to the neighbouring 'complement, not replace' sentence. Final: P41, unit_stance permit (AI is allowed under a condition), normalized policy kept because the anchor omits the opening of the sentence.

units.why: "Faculty members are best positioned to determine whether, when, and how AI tools support the learning objectives" hands the decision to faculty, so P04.
units.anchor: Faculty members are best positioned to determine whether, when, and how AI tools support
units.frag_end: of their respective courses and disciplines.

units.why: "appropriate uses of AI will vary across courses, programs, and professions" justifies variation by course and discipline, so the rule is set locally: P04. P11 (no carryover) is not stated.
units.anchor: appropriate uses of AI will vary across courses, programs, and professions
units.resolution_why: Coder A: actor all; coder B: admin. The sentence is a statement by the university about why it does not set one rule ('appropriate uses of AI will vary across courses, programs, and professions'), not an instruction to a particular group. Final: admin, consistent with the other P04 statements of the university in this document.

units.why: "affirms the role of faculty judgment in establishing expectations for AI use in their courses" is the university deferring to instructors: P04.
units.anchor: affirms the role of faculty judgment in establishing expectations for AI use in their courses
units.frag_start: Saint Joseph’s University affirms the role
units.resolution_why: Coder A: phase before-course; coder B: general. The sentence 'Saint Joseph's University affirms the role of faculty judgment' is a statement of the university's framework, not a step in course design. Final: general.

units.why: "Faculty should communicate clear guidance to students about when AI may be used" asks instructors to state expectations to students, which is P09.
units.anchor: Faculty should communicate clear guidance to students about when AI may be used
units.fit_note: A should, not a mandatory syllabus statement; it asks for guidance on when and how AI may be used and when it is not, without naming the syllabus. Coder B added: Asks for clear guidance on when AI may be used, how, and when it is inconsistent with the course, but names no syllabus or assignment statement.

units.why: "Our goal is not to prescribe a single approach to AI adoption" states the university sets no single rule and leaves it to instructors: P04.
units.anchor: Our goal is not to prescribe a single approach to AI adoption
units.policy: The University does not prescribe a single approach to AI adoption and encourages thoughtful engagement grounded in learning goals and disciplinary expertise

units.why: "Students should develop the ability to evaluate AI-generated information" is an expectation to evaluate AI output, matching P31 (verify output) more than P70 since no training is offered here.
units.anchor: Students should develop the ability to evaluate AI-generated information, recognize potential biases
units.fit_note: Also names recognizing bias, understanding ethical implications and exercising judgment as outcomes, wider than verifying output. Coder B added: Framed as a literacy goal students should develop, also covering ethical implications and judgment, not only checking output.

units.why: "students should understand and evaluate the cost to our environment" names environmental harm, P53.
units.anchor: students should understand and evaluate the cost to our environment

units.why: "AI will increasingly shape the professions and communities into which our graduates enter" gives the career reason for engaging with AI: P44.
units.anchor: AI will increasingly shape the professions and communities into which our graduates enter
units.resolution_why: Only coder A coded this. 'AI will increasingly shape the professions and communities into which our graduates enter' is a stated reason for AI literacy and is not a repeat of another sentence. Kept as a rationale unit (P44).

units.why: "It requires helping them to understand the capabilities, limitations, and implications of these technologies" commits the institution to AI-literacy education; P70 fits better than P44 because it concerns teaching AI literacy.
units.anchor: It requires helping them to understand the capabilities, limitations, and implications of these technologies.
units.fit_note: Stated as a requirement of preparation, not as a concrete training offering or mandate.

units.why: "They will understand the need to evaluate it, know when to challenge it" ties graduate success to human judgment over AI, a career-skill rationale, P44.
units.anchor: know when to challenge it, and the ways in which human judgment is indispensable
units.fit_note: Stresses evaluating and challenging AI and human judgment as the professional skill, more than using AI effectively.

units.why: "AI tools do not replace responsibility for the work we produce" says people own what they produce: P29.
units.anchor: AI tools do not replace responsibility for the work we produce.
units.resolution_why: Only coder A coded this as its own unit; coder B folded it into the next unit. 'AI tools do not replace responsibility for the work we produce' is a separate sentence from the faculty and student accountability sentence. Kept (P29, informs).

units.why: "accountable for the accuracy, quality, and integrity of their work, regardless of the extent of AI’s role" states accountability for work regardless of AI use, for students and faculty; P29.
units.anchor: accountable for the accuracy, quality, and integrity of their work, regardless of the extent

units.why: The list item "thoughtful evaluation of AI-generated content" is a minimum for responsible use ("requires, at minimum"), so verification: P31.
units.anchor: thoughtful evaluation of AI-generated content;
units.frag_start: Responsible academic use of AI requires,
units.policy: Responsible academic use of AI requires, at minimum, thoughtful evaluation of AI-generated content

units.why: "adherence to University academic integrity expectations" requires AI use to follow integrity rules; this is compliance with existing policy, P77 (not P45 since AI is not likened to a collaborator).
units.anchor: adherence to University academic integrity expectations;
units.frag_start: Responsible academic use of AI requires,
units.policy: Responsible academic use of AI requires, at minimum, adherence to University academic integrity expectations
units.resolution_why: Coder A: phase during-work; coder B: general. The list says what 'responsible academic use of AI requires, at minimum', and the three items are conditions on doing the work with AI, as are the sibling items on evaluation and respect. Final: during-work, for consistency across the three list items.

units.why: "respect for intellectual property, privacy, and ethical standards" is a minimum for responsible use; it spans IP, privacy and ethics, with P52 chosen because IP is named first and P50 covers only privacy and vetted tools.
units.anchor: respect for intellectual property, privacy, and ethical standards.
units.frag_start: Responsible academic use of AI requires,
units.policy: Responsible academic use of AI requires, at minimum, respect for intellectual property, privacy, and ethical standards
units.fit_note: Combines IP, privacy and ethical standards in one requirement; P52 covers only the IP part. Coder B added: P50 (privacy) and P53 (ethics) fit parts of it too; the clause combines IP, privacy and ethical standards in one requirement. Coder B added: Combines intellectual property, privacy and ethical standards in one clause; type P50 covers only privacy and vetted tools.
units.resolution_why: Coder A: P52, during-work; coder B: P50, general. The item 'respect for intellectual property, privacy, and ethical standards' names three concerns and fits no single type fully. IP is named first and P52 is the type for copyright and ownership; P50 covers only privacy and vetted tools. Final: P52 with a fit note, during-work as for the sibling items.

units.why: "The landscape of artificial intelligence will continue to evolve" signals that the guidance will change over time: P54.
units.anchor: The landscape of artificial intelligence will continue to evolve.
units.fit_note: Also commits to supporting faculty, students and staff in exploring AI, not only to revisiting the principles.

units.why: "committed to supporting faculty, students, and staff as they explore the opportunities and challenges" is a general support commitment that names no training, workshops or resources, so it fits neither P63 (faculty) nor P70 (training) and is left UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: committed to supporting faculty, students, and staff as they explore the opportunities and challenges
units.uncovered_note: The university commits in general terms to supporting faculty, students and staff as they explore AI, without naming any training or resources.
units.resolution_why: Only coder A coded this. 'committed to supporting faculty, students, and staff as they explore the opportunities and challenges' is a real commitment, separate from the 'landscape will continue to evolve' sentence, but names no training or resources, so P63 and P70 do not fit. Kept as UNCOVERED; coder B only noted it as a fit_note on the P54 unit.

documents.unit: Initiative for Human Formation in an Age of AI
documents.title: Saint Joseph's University's Guiding Principles for AI
documents.stance_why: The page states "They are not a policy" but "values that should guide judgment" in coursework, teaching, research and operations. It sets no stance on whether AI is allowed and refers disclosure to "University policy (including course or syllabus requirements)", so delegates.
documents.summary: Six university-wide principles (people-centered, privacy, fairness and bias, care for the environment, accountability, transparency) guide AI use across coursework, teaching, research and operations. The page says it is not a policy and does not replace existing data, privacy or integrity policies.

units.why: 'clear understanding of how AI is reshaping the workplace and the professions our graduates will enter' gives the career rationale, so P44.
units.anchor: a clear understanding of how AI is reshaping the workplace and the professions
units.frag_start: we are committed to providing our community
units.fit_note: Commits the university to informing the community about AI in work, rather than saying courses teach AI use.
units.resolution_why: Only coder B coded this. 'we are committed to providing our community with a clear understanding of how AI is reshaping the workplace and the professions our graduates will enter' is a stated commitment with a career rationale, not a repeat of another sentence. Kept (P44) with coder B's fit note.

units.why: "They are not a policy, and do not replace the University's existing policies on data, privacy, or academic integrity" states the status and scope of the principles, not an instruction to comply, so P56.
units.anchor: do not replace the University's existing policies on data, privacy, or academic integrity.
units.resolution_why: Coder A: P56, actor admin; coder B: P77, actor all. The sentence says the principles are not a policy and leave existing policies in place. It states the framework's status and does not itself tell anyone to comply, so P56 (framework scope), addressed by the university to the community: admin.

units.why: "the values that should guide judgment whenever members of our community use AI" defines what the principles are and where they apply, so scope, P56, informs.
units.anchor: the values that should guide judgment whenever members of our community use AI
units.resolution_why: Coder A: modality should; coder B: informs. The sentence defines the principles ('They are the values that...') and their scope in coursework, teaching, research and operations; the 'should' belongs to the relative clause describing the values. Final: informs.

units.why: "AI may support this development, but it cannot substitute for it" says AI is limited because human capacities are built by the person, the skill-building rationale: P41.
units.anchor: AI may support this development, but it cannot substitute for it.
units.resolution_why: Coder A: P41; coder B: P32. 'AI may support this development, but it cannot substitute for it' follows a list of human capacities students must develop, and gives the reason AI cannot do that work for them. That is the skill-building rationale, P41; the rule that people stay the thinker is coded at 'AI should augment human capability, not replace it'.

units.why: Principle 1 says 'AI should augment human capability, not replace it', so people must remain the thinkers: P32.
units.anchor: AI should augment human capability, not replace it.
units.resolution_why: Only coder B coded 'AI should augment human capability, not replace it' as its own unit; coder A coded the next sentence (P41) from the same passage. It is a separate rule that people stay the thinker. Kept (P32).

units.why: Principle 1 says members "should use AI in ways that strengthen their thinking and their work", which sets a condition on use and keeps the person as the thinker: P32. The second half of the sentence is coded separately.
units.anchor: should use AI in ways that strengthen their thinking and their work
units.policy: Members of our community should use AI in ways that strengthen their thinking and their work
units.resolution_why: Coder A: one P32 unit with the whole sentence; coder B: P31 unit covering only 'remain responsible for analyzing, questioning, and evaluating outcomes'. The sentence holds two rules, and one policy per unit is required. Final: P32 for 'strengthen their thinking and their work' and a separate P31 unit for the responsibility to evaluate outcomes.

units.why: 'remain responsible for analyzing, questioning, and evaluating outcomes' makes users keep the judging role over AI output: P31.
units.anchor: remain responsible for analyzing, questioning, and evaluating outcomes
units.frag_start: Members of our community should use AI
units.resolution_why: Coder A: one P32 unit with the whole sentence; coder B: P31 unit covering only 'remain responsible for analyzing, questioning, and evaluating outcomes'. The sentence holds two rules, and one policy per unit is required. Final: P32 for 'strengthen their thinking and their work' and a separate P31 unit for the responsibility to evaluate outcomes.

units.why: "The value of a university education rests on the development of a person's own reasoning, judgment, and skill" explains why AI should not replace thinking: P41.
units.anchor: The value of a university education rests on the development of a person's own reasoning
units.resolution_why: Only coder A coded this sentence ('The value of a university education rests on the development of a person's own reasoning, judgment, and skill'); coder B coded only the preceding sentence. It is a rationale for why AI should not replace thinking, not a repeat. Kept (P41).

units.why: Principle 2: "AI users must protect the privacy of others and sensitive or confidential University information" is a data-protection duty: P50.
units.anchor: AI users must protect the privacy of others and sensitive or confidential University information.
units.resolution_why: Actor, phase, modality and type agree. Unit stance: coder A neutral, coder B restrict. A duty to protect others' private data does not set a position on AI use itself, so neutral.

units.why: "ensure the use is consistent with all applicable laws, regulations and University Policies" requires legal and policy compliance for people with data access: P77.
units.anchor: ensure the use is consistent with all applicable laws, regulations and
units.policy: Those with access to data and tools must handle others' Personally Identifiable Information with care and ensure the use is consistent with all applicable laws, regulations and University Policies
units.fit_note: Mainly about PII handling by people with data access; the compliance clause is the P77 element.

units.why: "understanding the distinction between data use in enterprise-approved AI tools and free or personal subscriptions" points users to vetted enterprise tools over personal ones: P50.
units.anchor: the distinction between data use in enterprise-approved AI tools and free or personal subscriptions
units.policy: Members of our community should be mindful about what information they share with AI tools, understanding the distinction between data use in enterprise-approved AI tools and free or personal subscriptions

units.why: "Information entered into a public AI tool may not stay private" is a fact about tools retaining prompts: P50.
units.anchor: Information entered into a public AI tool may not stay private.

units.why: Principle 3: "AI outcomes should be evaluated for bias and unequal treatment" names bias; P53, with a note that access is equity (P51).
units.anchor: AI outcomes should be evaluated for bias and unequal treatment
units.policy: AI outcomes should be evaluated for bias and unequal treatment, in the results an AI tool produces and in who has access to the tool
units.fit_note: Also raises unequal access to the tool, which is equity (P51) rather than bias alone. Coder B added: Also extends bias to unequal access to the tool itself, which touches P51.

units.why: "consider who benefits and who might be disadvantaged by a given use of AI" asks users to weigh harms to groups: P53.
units.anchor: consider who benefits and who might be disadvantaged by a given use of AI
units.frag_end: the people and groups it touches.

units.why: Principle 4: "AI use carries a cost to the global environment we share" names an environmental cost: P53.
units.anchor: we recognize that AI use carries a cost to the global environment we share
units.resolution_why: Only coder A coded this sentence ('we recognize that AI use carries a cost to the global environment we share'); coder B folded it into the next unit's why. It names an environmental cost and is separate from the 'use AI deliberately' rule. Kept (P53, informs).

units.why: "use AI deliberately rather than reflexively" and "prefer simpler, less resource-intensive means" discourages casual AI use without forbidding it: P03.
units.anchor: should prefer simpler, less resource-intensive means when appropriate
units.frag_start: use AI deliberately rather than reflexively,
units.policy: Members of our community should use AI deliberately rather than reflexively, weighing the resource cost of a given use against the benefit it provides, and should prefer simpler, less resource-intensive means when appropriate
units.fit_note: Discourages reflexive use for environmental reasons; P03 captures the discouragement but not the resource-cost reason.
units.resolution_why: Coder A: P03; coder B: P53. The passage says members 'should use AI deliberately rather than reflexively' and 'prefer simpler, less resource-intensive means when appropriate'. That is a discouragement of casual use without a ban (P03); the environmental cost itself is coded as P53 in the previous unit. Final: P03 with a fit note that the reason is resource cost.

units.why: Principle 5: "Anyone who uses AI is responsible for the outcome", ownership of what one produces: P29.
units.anchor: Anyone who uses AI is responsible for the outcome

units.why: "its output must be reviewed and verified, not taken on faith, before it is relied upon" requires verifying AI output because it "can be wrong, biased": P31.
units.anchor: its output must be reviewed and verified, not taken on faith
units.resolution_why: Coder A: phase general; coder B: during-work. The sentence says AI output 'must be reviewed and verified, not taken on faith, before it is relied upon', which applies as people work with AI output. Final: during-work.

units.why: "This responsibility cannot be delegated to any tool" restates that accountability stays with the person: P29.
units.anchor: This responsibility cannot be delegated to any tool.
units.resolution_why: Only coder A coded 'This responsibility cannot be delegated to any tool' as its own unit. It restates accountability in a separate sentence, so it is kept (P29, informs).

units.why: Principle 6: "Use of AI should be disclosed when expected by University policy (including course or syllabus requirements)" makes disclosure conditional on other rules: P24.
units.anchor: Use of AI should be disclosed when expected by University policy
units.frag_start: Use of AI should be disclosed
units.fit_note: Disclosure applies only where policy, grant, publisher or law expects it; no general duty. Coder B added: Disclosure is conditional on university, course, publisher, funder or legal requirements rather than required for every submission.
units.resolution_why: Type, actor, phase and modality agree. Unit stance: coder A permit, coder B neutral. Disclosure is made conditional on other rules and sets no position on AI use, so neutral.

units.why: "be able to explain how AI contributed to their work and how they exercised their own judgment" asks people to explain AI's contribution when disclosure is required. P30 is nearest; P24 is disclosure itself.
units.anchor: be able to explain how AI contributed to their work
units.frag_start: When disclosure is required, members of
units.policy: When disclosure is required, members of our community should follow the requirements and be able to explain how AI contributed to their work and how they exercised their own judgment, verification and accountability
units.fit_note: Asks for explaining AI's contribution and one's own judgment, not explaining every line of code. Coder B added: Asks for explaining how AI contributed and how judgment was used, when disclosure is required, not every line of work.

notes: Reconciled from coders A and B (v2/run). Both documents are principles that the university says are not a policy; no school or computing policy found, course layer deferred. Main disagreements: P41 vs P32, P56 vs P77 for scope statements, and the three-concern IP/privacy/ethics clause.
